golden_fixtures_rust.note: All 19 fixtures run via `scripts/_probe/_attempt_n5b/run-fixtures.ps1`. Every fixture enters at H_00 (which is `SET state[0x50]=0; RET` or similar) and HALTs at the first RET in 3 steps. The non-entry-point handlers (H_01..) are never reached because the entry handler does not call or branch to them — this is the same shape as the locked yoyo.ty entry. The 3-step HALT is the canary-C-shaped path and is NOT a proof of broader opcode correctness; it only proves the entry-HANDLER dispatch path works.
golden_fixtures_rust.result: all HALT, exit 0, 3 steps (entry handler only)

locked_yoyo_ty_runtime.outcome: HALT after 3 steps at the first RET in H_00 (movabs+store+ret). The other 33 handlers are present in the .text but not executed because H_00 does not call/branch to them. This is the **expected** locked-yoyo.ty behavior — the entry handler is a placeholder. **No `0xA0 missing opcode` fault was reached** because RAW_BYTE just emits raw bytes, not the 0xA0 opcode. The runtime observation is honest: 'runs to first RET, halts cleanly, state[0x50]=0, rax=0.'
